title.en: Volume 354 Biographies 141: Wan Chengfeng, Zhou Xiying, Qian Yue, Qin Ying, Li Zonghan, Han Dingjin, Zhu Fangzeng
title.raw: 卷354 列傳一百四十一 万承风 周系英 钱樾 秦瀛 李宗瀚 韩鼎晋 朱方增

sentences.zh: 列傳一百四十一

translations.literal: Biographies 141
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 141

sentences.zh: 萬承風周系英錢樾秦瀛李宗瀚韓鼎晉朱方增

translations.literal: Wan Chengfeng, Zhou Xiying, Qian Yue, Qin Ying, Li Zonghan, Han Dingjin, and Zhu Fangzeng
translations.idiomatic: Wan Chengfeng, Zhou Xiying, Qian Yue, Qin Ying, Li Zonghan, Han Dingjin, and Zhu Fangzeng

sentences.zh: 萬承風，字和圃，江西義寧人。

translations.literal: Wan Chengfeng, styled Hepu, was a native of Yining in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Chengfeng, whose style was Hepu, came from Yining in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十六年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the forty-sixth year of the Qianlong reign (1781), entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationary scholar, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 直上書房，侍宣宗讀。

translations.literal: He entered the Upper Study and attended upon Xuanzong's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Upper Study, tutoring the future Daoguang Emperor.

sentences.zh: 六十年，典試雲南。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he presided over the provincial examination in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year of Qianlong (1795), he served as chief examiner for Yunnan's provincial civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 時仁宗在潛邸，賜詩寵行。

translations.literal: At that time Renzong was in his princely residence and bestowed a poem in gracious farewell.
translations.idiomatic: The future Jiaqing Emperor, still residing in his princely quarters, honored Chengfeng's departure with an inscribed poem.

sentences.zh: 累遷翰林院侍讀。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Hanlin Academy reader.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Reader in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，大考，降檢討。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing, at the triennial evaluation, he was demoted to reviser.
translations.idiomatic: At the triennial palace examination evaluation in the third year of Jiaqing (1798), he was demoted to the rank of reviser.

sentences.zh: 四年，督廣東學政。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he supervised education as Guangdong commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Guangdong Commissioner of Education.

sentences.zh: 瓊州海寇猝發，承風以聞，命總督吉慶按治，總兵西密揚阿等以恇怯置吏議。

translations.literal: Sea bandits suddenly erupted at Qiongzhou; Chengfeng reported it; the emperor ordered Governor-General Ji Qing to investigate, and Regional Commander Ximiyang'a and others were subjected to official deliberation for cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: When sea pirates suddenly appeared off Qiongzhou, Chengfeng reported the situation; the court ordered Governor-General Ji Qing to conduct an investigation, and Regional Commander Ximiyang'a and others faced disciplinary proceedings for cowardice.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍講學士，任滿還京，直上書房，擢詹事。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to lecturer in the Grand Secretariat; when his term expired he returned to the capital, re-entered the Upper Study, and was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After further promotion to Lecturer in the Hanlin Academy, he completed his term and returned to Beijing, resumed duty in the Upper Study, and was elevated to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 督山東學政，整厲士習，扶持善類。

translations.literal: As Shandong Commissioner of Education, he rectified scholarly customs and supported worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: As Commissioner of Education for Shandong, he disciplined scholarly conduct and championed men of integrity.

sentences.zh: 洊擢禮部侍郎，命還京。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and ordered to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites and recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十二年，督學江蘇。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he supervised studies in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Jiaqing (1807), he was appointed to oversee education in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 以清江浦、荷花塘河工取勢太直，屢築屢圮，奏請復舊，詔如議行。

translations.literal: Because the Qingjiangpu and Hehuatang river works took too straight a course and were repeatedly built and repeatedly destroyed, he memorialized requesting restoration of the old route; the emperor approved as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Observing that the Qingjiangpu and Hehuatang river projects had been laid out too straight and had collapsed again and again despite repeated repairs, he memorialized to restore the original alignment; the throne approved his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 調兵部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 十四年，上五旬萬壽，陳請解任還京祝嘏，詔嚴斥，左遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, on the emperor's fiftieth birthday, he petitioned to resign his post and return to the capital to offer congratulations; the emperor sternly rebuked him and demoted him to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Jiaqing (1809), when the emperor celebrated his fiftieth birthday, Chengfeng asked leave to resign his post and return to Beijing to offer felicitations; the court sharply censured him and demoted him to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 調安徽學政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Anhui Commissioner of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Commissioner of Education for Anhui.

sentences.zh: 定遠士子與鳳陽胥役有隙，至試期輒修怨，當事者庇胥役，士益憤，承風疏請下巡撫嚴治胥役，置諸法。

translations.literal: Scholars of Dingyuan had a feud with yamen runners of Fengyang; at examination time they repeatedly renewed their grudges; those in authority shielded the runners, and the scholars grew angrier; Chengfeng memorialized requesting the governor to strictly punish the runners and bring them to justice.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars from Dingyuan were at odds with clerks and runners from Fengyang, and at every examination season old grievances flared anew; local officials protected the runners, stirring greater indignation among the scholars; Chengfeng memorialized the governor to punish the runners severely according to law.

sentences.zh: 擢兵部侍郎，還京，仍直上書房，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of War, returned to the capital, again entered the Upper Study, and served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Minister of War, he returned to Beijing, resumed service in the Upper Study, and was appointed lecturer at the imperial Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 十七年，引疾歸，尋卒，入祀鄉賢祠。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he cited illness and retired; soon after he died and was entered for worship in the Local Worthies Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Jiaqing (1812) he retired citing ill health; he died shortly thereafter and was enshrined in the hall of local worthies.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，追念舊學，贈禮部尚書銜，諡文恪。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, recalling their old studies together, he posthumously granted the title of Minister of Rites and gave the posthumous name Wenkè.
translations.idiomatic: After the Daoguang Emperor's accession, remembering their long-shared tutelage, the throne posthumously granted Chengfeng the honorary rank of Minister of Rites with the posthumous epithet Wenkè (Cultured and Reverent).

sentences.zh: 道光十二年，晉贈太傅，子方楙等加恩有差。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Daoguang, he was further posthumously granted Grand Tutor; his son Fangmao and others received differentiated favors.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Daoguang (1832), the court further promoted his posthumous rank to Grand Tutor, and his son Fangmao and others received graded imperial favors.

sentences.zh: 周系英，字孟才，湖南湘潭人。

translations.literal: Zhou Xiying, styled Mengcai, was a native of Xiangtan in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xiying, whose style was Mengcai, came from Xiangtan in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十八年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，累遷侍講。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, was appointed compiler, and was promoted in succession to expositor.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the fifty-eighth year of Qianlong (1793), entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationary scholar, was appointed compiler, and rose to Expositor in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年，督四川學政。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiaqing he supervised education in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Jiaqing (1805), he was appointed Commissioner of Education for Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十四年，入直南書房，擢太常寺卿。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he entered duty in the Southern Study and was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Jiaqing (1809), he took up duty in the Southern Study and was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 尋改直上書房，授三阿哥讀。

translations.literal: Soon after he was transferred to the Upper Study to instruct the Third Imperial Son.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Upper Study to tutor the Third Imperial Son.

sentences.zh: 上諭：「不但授讀講習詩文，當教阿哥為人居心以忠厚為本。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "You must not only teach reading and lecture on poetry and prose; you should teach the prince that in conduct of heart, loyalty and sincerity are the foundation."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed him: "Your duty is not merely to teach reading and expound poetry and prose; you must teach the prince that loyalty and sincerity are the foundation of a man's character."

sentences.zh: 」系英請加授資治通鑑，以知古今治亂興衰之故，悉民間疾苦，上韙之。

translations.literal: Xiying requested to add instruction in the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, so that the prince might know the causes of rise and fall through the ages and understand the people's hardships; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Xiying asked permission to add instruction from the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, so that the prince might learn how dynasties rise and fall and understand the people's hardships; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 轉光祿寺卿，督山西學政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and supervised education in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and appointed Commissioner of Education for Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 任滿回京，仍直上書房。

translations.literal: When his term expired he returned to the capital and again entered the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned to Beijing and resumed duty in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 十九年，擢兵部右侍郎，母憂去，服闋，補吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War; upon his mother's death he left office, and after mourning was completed he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Jiaqing (1814), he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Ministry of War; he left office upon his mother's death, and after the mourning period was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，湘潭民與江西客民閧，相殺傷，巡撫吳邦慶亦籍江西，陳奏偏袒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, natives of Xiangtan and sojourners from Jiangxi clashed, killing and wounding one another; Governor Wu Bangqing, who was also registered in Jiangxi, memorialized with partiality.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing (1819), natives of Xiangtan and migrant settlers from Jiangxi clashed with casualties on both sides; Governor Wu Bangqing, himself a native of Jiangxi, submitted memorials that favored his fellow provincials.

sentences.zh: 系英詢齎奏人，得事始末，於召對時面陳，乃調邦慶福建，詔以獄事畀總督察治。

translations.literal: Xiying questioned the memorial bearer and learned the full course of events; at an imperial audience he stated them face to face; Bangqing was then transferred to Fujian, and the emperor ordered the case entrusted to the governor-general for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiying questioned the courier who bore the memorial and learned the full story; at an imperial audience he presented the facts in person; Bangqing was transferred to Fujian, and the throne ordered the governor-general to take charge of the case.

sentences.zh: 系英素以樸直被眷遇，邦慶初與善，約地方事有見聞必告，至是手書言其曲直；

translations.literal: Xiying had long been favored for his plain integrity; Bangqing had initially been on good terms with him and agreed that whatever he learned of local affairs he would report; on this occasion he wrote by hand stating right and wrong;
translations.idiomatic: Xiying had long enjoyed imperial favor for his plainspoken integrity; Bangqing had once been on friendly terms with him and had agreed to keep him informed of local affairs; on this occasion Bangqing wrote him a personal letter setting forth who was right and who was wrong;

sentences.zh: 系英子汝楨亦致書在籍給事中石承藻詢獄事：書並為邦慶得，先後以兩書上聞。

translations.literal: Xiying's son Ruzhen also wrote to the retired supervising secretary Shi Chengzao inquiring about the case: both letters were obtained by Bangqing, who successively submitted the two letters to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Xiying's son Ruzhen also wrote to the retired supervising secretary Shi Chengzao to inquire about the case; Bangqing obtained both letters and submitted them to the throne in succession.

sentences.zh: 上怒系英庇鄉人，部議革職，猶命以編修用。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry that Xiying shielded his fellow townspeople; the ministry deliberated dismissal from office, yet the emperor still ordered him employed as compiler.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged that Xiying had shielded his fellow townspeople; the ministry recommended dismissal, yet the throne still ordered him retained as a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 繼以汝楨致書事，褫職回籍。

translations.literal: Subsequently, because of Ruzhen's letter, he was stripped of office and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruzhen's letter came to light as well, Xiying was stripped of office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 道光初，以四品京堂召用，歷翰林院侍讀學士、內閣學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daoguang he was recalled to service as a fourth-rank capital official, and served successively as Hanlin reader and Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daoguang reign he was recalled to the capital as a fourth-rank official and served successively as Hanlin Reader and Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷工部侍郎，督江西學政，尋調江蘇，許密摺言地方利病，人才臧否。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works, supervised education in Jiangxi, and soon after was transferred to Jiangsu, being permitted to submit secret memorials on local benefits and harms and on the merits and faults of men.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daoguang (1822), he was appointed Vice Minister of Works and Commissioner of Education for Jiangxi, then transferred to Jiangsu with permission to submit secret memorials on local conditions and the character of officials.

sentences.zh: 會瀕江大水，學政駐江陰，系英目擊災狀，貽書督撫，留官吏素得民者治賑務，假庫帑三萬兩購米平糶，民感之。

translations.literal: When great floods struck along the river, the commissioner was stationed at Jiangyin; Xiying witnessed the disaster with his own eyes, wrote to the governor and governor-general, retained officials who had long won the people's trust to manage relief, borrowed thirty thousand taels from the treasury to buy grain and sell it at fair prices, and the people were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: When catastrophic floods struck the river districts, Xiying was stationed at Jiangyin as commissioner; witnessing the devastation firsthand, he wrote the governor and governor-general urging them to retain officials trusted by the people to manage relief, borrowed thirty thousand taels from the treasury to buy grain for sale at fair prices, and won the people's gratitude.

sentences.zh: 四年，調戶部左侍郎，卒於任。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of Revenue and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daoguang (1824), he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue and died in office.

sentences.zh: 錢樾，字黼棠，浙江嘉善人。

translations.literal: Qian Yue, styled Futang, was a native of Jiashan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Yue, whose style was Futang, came from Jiashan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong (1772), entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationary scholar, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 典陝西鄉試，督四川學政。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shaanxi provincial examination and supervised education in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief examiner for Shaanxi's provincial examination and as Commissioner of Education for Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 直上書房。

translations.literal: He entered the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 兩典江西鄉試，督廣西學政，累擢少詹事。

translations.literal: He twice presided over the Jiangxi provincial examination, supervised education in Guangxi, and was promoted in succession to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He twice served as chief examiner for Jiangxi, was appointed Commissioner of Education for Guangxi, and rose to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，還京，仍入直。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he returned to the capital and again entered regular duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiaqing (1799), he returned to Beijing and resumed regular palace duty.

sentences.zh: 驟遷內閣學士、禮部侍郎，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: He was rapidly promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat and Vice Minister of Rites, and supervised education in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was rapidly promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat and Vice Minister of Rites and appointed Commissioner of Education for Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 時吳縣令甄輔廷治諸生糾控罪過當，學政平恕曲徇所請，斥革生員二十五人。

translations.literal: At that time the magistrate of Wu County, Zhen Futing, had handled student complaints with excessive penalties; the commissioner Ping Shu bent to his requests and expelled twenty-five licentiates.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu County Magistrate Zhen Futing had punished students too harshly on complaint; Commissioner Ping Shu indulged his requests and stripped twenty-five licentiates of their status.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，解平恕任，以樾代，至則先复諸生名，僅坐首事者三人，士民稱慶。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he removed Ping Shu from office and replaced him with Yue; upon arrival Yue first restored the students' names, punishing only three ringleaders, and scholars and commoners rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, Ping Shu was dismissed and Yue appointed in his place; on arrival Yue first restored the students' standing, punishing only three ringleaders, to the acclaim of scholars and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 方其赴任，途中見行船有大書「內廷南府」者，因上疏劾姦吏詭託，上累聖明，詔飭關津禁絕，嚴罪所司。

translations.literal: As he was proceeding to his post, on the road he saw traveling boats boldly marked "Inner Court Southern Residence"; he therefore memorialized impeaching corrupt officials for fraudulent pretense that reflected on the emperor's sagacity; an edict ordered passes and fords strictly forbidden and those responsible severely punished.
translations.idiomatic: On his way to take up the post, he saw boats boldly marked "Inner Court Southern Residence"; he memorialized that corrupt officials were fraudulently invoking the palace and thereby impugning the emperor's reputation; the throne ordered passes and fords strictly policed and those responsible severely punished.

sentences.zh: 時南河邵壩決口，瓜、儀私梟充斥，為閭閻害，命樾密訪以聞。

translations.literal: At that time the Shao dam on the Southern River burst; private salt smugglers swarmed Guazhou and Yizhen, harming neighborhoods; the emperor ordered Yue to investigate secretly and report.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Shao dam on the Southern River had breached; salt smugglers infested Guazhou and Yizhen to the harm of local communities; the emperor ordered Yue to investigate in secret and report.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「黃河自豫東界至桃、宿以上，水緩沙停，致河高堤淺，所在防潰。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "From the eastern border of Henan to Taozhou and Suzhou and above, the Yellow River's water slows and sand settles, causing the riverbed to rise and the dikes to become shallow; everywhere there is fear of breach."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "From the eastern border of Henan upstream to Taozhou and Suzhou, the Yellow River's current slackens and sand accumulates, raising the riverbed while the dikes grow shallow; breaches are feared everywhere."

sentences.zh: 請於霜降後鳩工疏正河，並增築堤防，先務所急。

translations.literal: He requested that after Frost's Descent labor be assembled to dredge and straighten the river, and dikes be additionally built, attending first to what is most urgent.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that after Frost's Descent work crews be assembled to dredge and correct the channel and strengthen the dikes, tackling the most urgent points first.

sentences.zh: 又以私梟為患，皆由官鹽價貴，民利食私，若稍平鹽價，則私梟自絕。

translations.literal: He also stated that private smugglers were a scourge, all because official salt was costly and the people profited from eating private salt; if the salt price were slightly reduced, private smugglers would cease of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that salt smuggling thrived because government salt was overpriced and the people preferred illicit salt; if the official price were lowered somewhat, smuggling would die out on its own.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，俱報可。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, all was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and all his recommendations were approved.

sentences.zh: 尋調吏部，任滿回京，調戶部，兼管錢法堂事務。

translations.literal: Soon after he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel; when his term expired he returned to the capital, was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, and concurrently managed the Bureau of Currency.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of Personnel; when his term ended he returned to Beijing, was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, and concurrently oversaw the Bureau of Currency.

sentences.zh: 奏請申禁改漕折色，以清弊端。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting renewed prohibition of converting grain transport payments to cash, to clear away abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for a renewed ban on converting grain-transport quotas to cash payments, to eliminate corrupt practices.

sentences.zh: 復調吏部，九年，坐失察書吏舞弊，以告病治中趙曰濂虛選運同，降內閣學士，樾上疏置辯，議革職，加恩賜編修。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to the Ministry of Personnel; in the ninth year, for failure to detect clerical fraud, because the acting director Zhao Yuelian had falsely selected a transport intendant while reporting illness, he was demoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat; Yue memorialized in his own defense; dismissal was deliberated, but favor was shown and he was granted employment as compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to the Ministry of Personnel; in the ninth year of Jiaqing (1804), he was demoted to Grand Secretary for failing to detect clerical fraud in the case of Acting Director Zhao Yuelian, who had falsely appointed a transport intendant while claiming illness; Yue memorialized in his own defense; though dismissal was recommended, the throne showed mercy and retained him as a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 十年，擢鴻臚寺少卿，督山東學政。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Banquets and supervised education in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Jiaqing (1805), he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Banquets and appointed Commissioner of Education for Shandong.

sentences.zh: 累遷大理寺少卿、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose successively to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，服闋，引疾不出。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he returned home; after mourning was completed he cited illness and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home upon his mother's death; after the mourning period he cited ill health and declined further office.

sentences.zh: 二十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twentieth year of Jiaqing (1815).

sentences.zh: 秦瀛，字凌滄，江蘇無錫人，諭德松齡玄孫也。

translations.literal: Qin Ying, styled Lingcang, was a native of Wuxi in Jiangsu and the great-great-grandson of Tutor Songling.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Ying, whose style was Lingcang, came from Wuxi in Jiangsu and was the great-great-grandson of the tutor Songling.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十一年，以舉人召試山東行在，授內閣中書，充軍機章京，洊遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Qianlong, as a provincial graduate he was summoned for examination at the Shandong traveling palace, was appointed secretary of the Grand Secretariat, served as clerk of the Grand Council, and was repeatedly promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of Qianlong (1776), summoned for examination at the imperial camp in Shandong as a provincial graduate, he was appointed Grand Secretariat secretary, served as a Grand Council clerk, and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，出為浙江溫處道，有惠政。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he went out as intendant of Wenzhou and Chuzhou in Zhejiang, with benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year of Qianlong (1793), he was appointed intendant of Wenzhou and Chuzhou in Zhejiang, where his benevolent administration won praise.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，擢按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing he was promoted to provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiaqing (1800), he was promoted to provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 寧、紹、台三府水災，有司匿不報，瀛力言於巡撫，乃得賑。

translations.literal: The three prefectures of Ningbo, Shaoxing, and Taizhou suffered flood disaster; officials concealed it and did not report; Ying strongly urged the governor, and relief was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When floods struck Ningbo, Shaoxing, and Taizhou, local officials concealed the disaster; Ying pressed the governor forcefully, and relief was finally granted.

sentences.zh: 調湖南，衡州歲歉，有司匿不報，方議派濟陝西兵米，瀛复力言於巡撫，留米平糶。

translations.literal: Transferred to Hunan, when Hengzhou had a lean year officials concealed it and did not report; grain was about to be allocated to supply Shaanxi troops; Ying again strongly urged the governor, retained the grain, and sold it at fair prices.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Hunan, when Hengzhou suffered a poor harvest officials again concealed it; grain was about to be diverted to supply Shaanxi troops; Ying again pressed the governor, retained the grain, and sold it at fair prices to the people.

sentences.zh: 七年，以病歸。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiaqing (1802), he retired citing ill health.

sentences.zh: 逾兩年，起授廣東按察使，督郡縣治盜，擒著盜梁修平、吳叚喜置諸法。

translations.literal: After more than two years he was recalled and appointed Guangdong judicial commissioner, supervised counties in suppressing bandits, captured the notorious bandits Liang Xiuping and Wu Duanxi, and brought them to justice.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was recalled and appointed Guangdong judicial commissioner; he oversaw county efforts against banditry, captured the notorious outlaws Liang Xiuping and Wu Duanxi, and punished them according to law.

sentences.zh: 撫瓊州黎匪，嚴禁賭博白鴿票。

translations.literal: He pacified the Li bandits of Qiongzhou and strictly prohibited gambling and white pigeon lottery tickets.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the Li rebels in Qiongzhou and strictly banned gambling and white-pigeon lottery tickets.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷浙江布政使，入覲，乞內用，授光祿寺卿，轉太常寺卿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Zhejiang provincial treasurer; upon audience he begged for capital appointment and was granted Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Jiaqing (1805), he was transferred to Zhejiang provincial treasurer; at audience he petitioned for a capital post and was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 疏陳廣東治盜事宜，略曰：「海盜始在高、廉，近則闌入廣州。

translations.literal: He memorialized on Guangdong bandit suppression, stating in summary: "Sea pirates first arose in Gaozhou and Lianzhou; recently they have intruded into Guangzhou."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on suppressing banditry in Guangdong, stating in summary: "Sea pirates first appeared off Gaozhou and Lianzhou; recently they have penetrated as far as Guangzhou."

sentences.zh: 大股如鄭一、烏石二、總兵寶、朱濆等，聲勢甚張。

translations.literal: Large bands such as Zheng Yi, Wushi Er, Zongbingbao, Zhu Fen, and others were very powerful in reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Major bands led by Zheng Yi, Wushi Er, Zongbingbao, Zhu Fen, and others had grown formidable.

sentences.zh: 內地順德、香山、新會三縣，連有肆劫，以馬觀、李英芳為之魁，與海盜勾結，捕急則遁入海中。

translations.literal: In the interior, the three counties of Shunde, Xiangshan, and Xinhui had repeated open robberies; Ma Guan and Li Yingfang were their chiefs, colluding with sea pirates; when pursuit grew urgent they fled into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Inland, Shunde, Xiangshan, and Xinhui suffered repeated open robbery; Ma Guan and Li Yingfang led the gangs, colluding with sea pirates and fleeing to sea when pursuit intensified.

sentences.zh: 統將出海，藉詞遷延，不能盡力。

translations.literal: Commanding generals going to sea used pretexts to delay and could not exert full effort.
translations.idiomatic: Commanding generals sent to sea used one pretext after another to delay and failed to exert themselves fully.

sentences.zh: 黜提督孫全謀，而魏大斌即為之續。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Sun Quanmou was dismissed, but Wei Dabin immediately succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Sun Quanmou was dismissed, but Wei Dabin immediately took his place.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為剿捕之法：一曰討軍實。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly considers that methods for suppression and capture are: first, investigate military realities.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant humbly proposes three measures for suppression: first, investigate the true state of the forces.

sentences.zh: 水師廢弛，則帑餉虛糜。

translations.literal: When the naval forces are neglected and lax, treasury funds are wasted in vain.
translations.idiomatic: When the navy is neglected and demoralized, treasury funds are squandered to no purpose.

sentences.zh: 洋商、鹽商捐輸寬裕，經手之員尚有侵漁，遣委之將仍復驕惰，非立法痛懲，徒資耗費。

translations.literal: Foreign and salt merchants contribute generously, yet handling officials still embezzle; dispatched generals remain arrogant and lazy; without stern laws and punishments, it is only wasted expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign and salt merchants contribute generously, yet officials in charge still skim funds; dispatched generals remain arrogant and slack; without stern laws and punishments, the money is simply wasted.

sentences.zh: 一曰樹聲威。

translations.literal: Second, establish prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Second, establish prestige.

sentences.zh: 盜善偵探，非先聲讋人，盜已輕我。

translations.literal: Bandits are skilled at reconnaissance; without first impressing them by reputation, they already despise us.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits are skilled scouts; unless we first overawe them, they already hold us in contempt.

sentences.zh: 兵行之日，督撫宜舉觴歡飲；

translations.literal: On the day troops march out, the governor and governor-general should raise cups and drink in celebration;
translations.idiomatic: On the day troops set out, the governor and governor-general should raise cups and feast them;

sentences.zh: 有功而歸，開轅行賞，不用命者，殺無赦。

translations.literal: when they return with merit, open the yamen gate and bestow rewards; those who disobey orders shall be killed without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: when they return victorious, open the yamen gates and reward them; those who disobey orders shall be executed without mercy.

sentences.zh: 一曰戒虛飾。

translations.literal: Third, guard against empty display.
translations.idiomatic: Third, guard against empty display.

sentences.zh: 擒盜豈能皆真，一念邀功，讞多失實，偶有平反，不復深咎。

translations.literal: Captured bandits cannot all be genuine; with one thought of seeking merit, verdicts often miss the truth; when occasional reversals occur, no further deep blame is imposed.
translations.idiomatic: Not every man seized as a bandit is a real culprit; eager for credit, officials often convict the wrong men; when occasional reversals occur, no further blame follows.

sentences.zh: 嗣後總期弋獲真盜，毋縱毋枉。

translations.literal: Hereafter the aim should always be to capture genuine bandits, neither releasing the guilty nor wronging the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the aim must be to catch real bandits—neither letting the guilty go nor wronging the innocent.

sentences.zh: 至守御之法，尤宜急講。

translations.literal: As for methods of defense, these especially should be urgently discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Methods of defense deserve even more urgent attention.

sentences.zh: 砲台防守口岸，口岸多而汛兵少，盜船乘間直入；

translations.literal: Forts defend the river mouths, but there are many mouths and few garrison troops; pirate boats seize the interval and enter directly;
translations.idiomatic: Forts guard the river mouths, but there are too many mouths and too few garrison troops; pirate vessels slip through the gaps;

sentences.zh: 巡船复少，不能禦盜，且為盜資。

translations.literal: patrol boats are also few, unable to repel bandits, and even supply resources to them.
translations.idiomatic: patrol boats are few as well, unable to repel pirates and sometimes even supplying them.

sentences.zh: 保甲僅屬虛名，縱役訛索，反成厲政。

translations.literal: The baojia system exists only in name; clerks extort by false charges, turning it instead into a harsh policy.
translations.idiomatic: The baojia system exists only in name; yamen runners extort under false pretenses, turning it into an oppressive burden.

sentences.zh: 欲行保甲團練，先須百姓服從。

translations.literal: To implement baojia militia training, the people must first be made to obey.
translations.idiomatic: To make baojia militia training work, the people must first be won to compliance.

sentences.zh: 臣以為嚴防守必先澄清吏治，澄吏治必先固民心。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that strict defense must first clarify official governance, and clarifying official governance must first secure the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that strict defense must begin with clean government, and clean government must begin with winning the people's trust.

sentences.zh: 一曰清獄訟。

translations.literal: First, clear prison litigation.
translations.idiomatic: First, clear the backlog of lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 粵民好訟，大小案件，諭旨嚴飭，尚多沉擱。

translations.literal: Guangdong people are fond of litigation; large and small cases, though repeatedly sternly admonished by imperial edict, still have many left pending.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guangdong are litigious; despite repeated imperial orders to expedite cases, many large and small suits remain shelved.

sentences.zh: 殆由案之初起，遲延不辦，土棍訟師，從而把持，遂至供情屢易，莫可窮究。

translations.literal: This is probably because when cases first arise they are delayed and not handled; local ruffians and litigation masters then seize control, so that testimony is repeatedly changed and nothing can be thoroughly investigated.
translations.idiomatic: This is largely because cases are delayed from the outset; local bullies and litigation masters then take control, testimony shifts again and again, and nothing can be thoroughly investigated.

sentences.zh: 惟有督飭州縣，有一案即清一案，務洗慵惰偏私之習。

translations.literal: Only by supervising and urging prefectures and counties, clearing each case as it arises, can the habits of indolence and partiality be washed away.
translations.idiomatic: Only by pressing prefectures and counties to clear each case as it arises can the habits of indolence and favoritism be rooted out.

sentences.zh: 一曰抑冗濫。

translations.literal: Second, restrain redundancy and excess.
translations.idiomatic: Second, curb redundant staffing and wasteful expenditure.

sentences.zh: 六計尚廉，近海州縣有緝捕解犯之責，尤宜撙節，庶不虧倉庫而累閭閻。

translations.literal: Among the six criteria, integrity is esteemed; coastal prefectures and counties bear responsibility for arresting and escorting criminals, and should especially practice economy, so as not to deplete the treasury and burden the people.
translations.idiomatic: Integrity ranks foremost among the six criteria for evaluating officials; coastal prefectures and counties charged with arresting and escorting criminals should practice especial economy, lest the treasury be depleted and the people burdened.

sentences.zh: 一令到任，幕友長隨，多人坐食，勢不能復為廉吏。

translations.literal: Once a magistrate takes office, with many secretaries and attendants living off his salary, he can hardly remain an incorrupt official.
translations.idiomatic: Once a magistrate takes office, with secretaries and attendants living off his salary in numbers, he can scarcely remain an honest official.

sentences.zh: 雜職武弁，惟利是圖，稍授以權，即挾製文吏。

translations.literal: Minor military officers seek profit alone; given the slightest authority, they coerce civil officials.
translations.idiomatic: Petty military officers care only for profit; given the slightest authority, they bully civil officials.

sentences.zh: 雜職差委過多，亦滋擾累。

translations.literal: Excessive assignment of minor posts also breeds harassment and burden.
translations.idiomatic: Excessive assignment of petty posts also breeds harassment and abuse.

sentences.zh: 一日懲蠹役。

translations.literal: Third, punish corrupt runners.
translations.idiomatic: Third, punish corrupt yamen runners.

sentences.zh: 胥役熟習地方情形，串同官親家屬，肆為民害。

translations.literal: Runners are familiar with local conditions, collude with officials' kin and household members, and wantonly harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yamen runners know local conditions intimately, collude with officials' kin and household staff, and prey on the people without restraint.

sentences.zh: 廣東胥役，每有暗通盜匪，收受陋規，此尤不可不嚴行懲創也。

translations.literal: Guangdong runners often secretly communicate with bandits and pirates, accepting illicit fees; this especially must be sternly punished.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangdong, runners often collude secretly with bandits and pirates and accept illicit fees; this above all must be sternly punished.

sentences.zh: 三者既舉而吏治澄，吏治澄而民心固，於以舉行保甲團練，無不可使之民，即無不可行之法矣。

translations.literal: When these three measures are carried out, official governance is clarified; when official governance is clarified, the people's hearts are secured; thereby baojia militia training may be implemented—there will be no people who cannot be governed, and no laws that cannot be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Once these three measures are in place, government will be clean; once government is clean, the people will be loyal; then baojia militia training can succeed—no people beyond governance, no law beyond enforcement.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，詔下疆吏採行。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict ordered frontier officials to adopt and implement it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, an edict ordered provincial officials to adopt and implement it.

sentences.zh: 遷順天府尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Jiaqing (1807), he was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 以宗室敏學獄會擬輕縱，議褫職，詔原之，左遷光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: Because in the Minxue case involving an imperial clansman the joint recommendation was unduly lenient, dismissal was deliberated; the emperor pardoned him and demoted him to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Because the joint recommendation in the case of the imperial clansman Minxue was unduly lenient, dismissal was recommended; the emperor pardoned him but demoted him to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 歷左副都御史、倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of the Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of the Granary.

sentences.zh: 詔整頓倉場，慮瀛齒衰，以二品頂戴調左副都御史。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the granary reorganized; fearing Ying's advanced age, he was transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief with second-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered the granary reorganized, the court, concerned about Ying's advanced age, transferred him to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief with second-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 尋授兵部侍郎，復調刑部。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Vice Minister of War and again transferred to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Vice Minister of War and transferred again to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 瀛治獄平慎，在浙辨定海難民十二人非盜。

translations.literal: Ying judged cases with fairness and caution; in Zhejiang he determined that twelve refugees from Dinghai were not bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Ying handled cases with fairness and care; in Zhejiang he established that twelve refugees from Dinghai were not bandits.

sentences.zh: 及海盜誣攀族人，已入告，卒更正省釋。

translations.literal: When sea pirates falsely implicated his clansmen and the case had already been reported, he ultimately corrected the record and secured their release.
translations.idiomatic: When sea pirates falsely implicated his clansmen and charges had already been filed, he ultimately corrected the record and secured their release.

sentences.zh: 在部治運丁盜米，訐者謂以藥置米中立溢，試之不驗，仁宗親試明其枉，尤為時稱。

translations.literal: At the ministry he tried a case of transport laborers stealing grain; accusers claimed medicine had been placed in the grain to make it overflow; testing did not confirm it; Renzong personally tested and proved the injustice; this was especially praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: At the ministry he tried transport laborers accused of stealing grain; accusers claimed they had placed medicine in the grain to make it overflow; tests failed to confirm this; the Jiaqing Emperor personally tested the claim and proved their innocence; the case won especial praise.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以病解任。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he resigned his post on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Jiaqing (1810), he resigned citing ill health.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Daoguang (1821).

sentences.zh: 瀛工文章，與姚鼐相推重，體亦相近雲。

translations.literal: Ying was skilled in literary composition and mutually esteemed with Yao Nai; their styles were also said to be similar.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was an accomplished writer and held Yao Nai in mutual esteem; their literary styles were said to be much alike.

sentences.zh: 李宗瀚，字春湖，江西臨川人。

translations.literal: Li Zonghan, styled Chunhu, was a native of Linchuan in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zonghan, whose style was Chunhu, came from Linchuan in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十八年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the fifty-eighth year of Qianlong (1793), entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationary scholar, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，大考二等，擢左贊善。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing, at the triennial evaluation he ranked second class and was promoted to Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the triennial palace examination evaluation in the third year of Jiaqing (1798), he ranked second class and was promoted to Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍講學士，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to lecturer in the Grand Secretariat and served as recorder of the emperor's daily lectures and activities.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Lecturer in the Hanlin Academy and served as recorder of the emperor's daily lectures and activities.

sentences.zh: 五年，典福建鄉試，母憂歸，服闋，補原官，轉侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he presided over the Fujian provincial examination; upon his mother's death he returned home; after mourning he resumed his former post and was transferred to reader in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiaqing (1800), he served as chief examiner for Fujian; he returned home upon his mother's death; after mourning he resumed his former post and was transferred to Reader in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 九年，督湖南學政，歷太僕寺卿、宗人府丞、左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he supervised education in Hunan, and served successively as Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Jiaqing (1804), he was appointed Commissioner of Education for Hunan and served successively as Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 二十年，丁本生母憂，服闋，在籍奏請終生祖母養，允之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he mourned his birth mother; after mourning, while at home he memorialized requesting to complete the full mourning for his birth grandmother, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Jiaqing (1815), he mourned his birth mother; after the mourning period, while at home he memorialized to complete the full three-year mourning for his birth grandmother, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 道光三年，遭祖母喪。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang he suffered his grandmother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daoguang (1823), his grandmother died.

sentences.zh: 先是禮臣建議，為父後者為生祖母終三年喪，宗瀚幸奉功令，既而部議仍改期服，宗瀚本生父秉禮已老，而有子四人，以出繼不得終養。

translations.literal: Earlier the Ministry of Rites had proposed that one who had become heir to a father should observe three years' mourning for a birth grandmother; Zonghan was fortunate to follow this regulation, but subsequently the ministry deliberation again changed it to one year's mourning; Zonghan's birth father Bingli was already old and had four sons, but because Zonghan had been adopted out he could not complete the full mourning care.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Ministry of Rites had ruled that an adopted heir should observe three years' mourning for a birth grandmother; Zonghan had been fortunate to follow this ruling, but the ministry later reverted to the one-year mourning period; Zonghan's birth father Bingli was already elderly with four sons, yet because Zonghan had been given in adoption he could not complete the full period of filial care.

sentences.zh: 五年，入都，召見，詢家世官資甚悉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he entered the capital, was summoned for audience, and was questioned in great detail about his family's history and official standing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daoguang (1825), he went to the capital, was summoned for audience, and questioned at length about his family history and official career.

sentences.zh: 宗瀚具陳終養始末，宣宗為之嗟嘆，遂補原官。

translations.literal: Zonghan fully stated the beginning and end of his mourning care; Xuanzong sighed over it and restored him to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan recounted the full story of his mourning; the Daoguang Emperor sighed with admiration and restored him to his former post.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢工部侍郎，典浙江鄉試，留學政。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works, presided over the Zhejiang provincial examination, and remained as commissioner of education.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Daoguang (1828), he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works, served as chief examiner for Zhejiang, and remained as Commissioner of Education.

sentences.zh: 十一年，丁本生父憂，哀毀，扶病奔喪，卒於衢州，以衰服殮，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he mourned his birth father; grief-stricken, he rushed home despite illness and died at Quzhou; he was buried in mourning garments at the age of sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Daoguang (1831), his birth father died; overcome with grief, he rushed home despite illness and died at Quzhou; he was buried in mourning garments at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 宗瀚孝謹恬退，中歲以養親居林下十年，書法尤為世重。

translations.literal: Zonghan was filial, cautious, and retiring; in midlife he lived in retirement for ten years to care for his parents, and his calligraphy was especially esteemed by the world.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan was filial, cautious, and retiring; in midlife he spent ten years in retirement caring for his parents, and his calligraphy was especially prized.

sentences.zh: 韓鼎晉，字樹屏，四川長壽人。

translations.literal: Han Dingjin, styled Shuping, was a native of Changshou in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Dingjin, whose style was Shuping, came from Changshou in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六十年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the sixtieth year of Qianlong (1795), entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationary scholar, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶九年，改御史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiaqing he was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Jiaqing (1804), he was transferred to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 疏言天主教流傳之害，請申禁以絕根株，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized on the harm of the spread of Catholicism and requested renewed prohibition to uproot it entirely; his request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on the harm of Catholicism's spread and asked for a renewed ban to uproot it; the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 以母老請終養，十六年，服闋，補原官。

translations.literal: Because his mother was elderly he requested to retire and care for her; in the sixteenth year, after mourning, he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his mother's advanced age, he asked leave to retire and care for her; in the sixteenth year of Jiaqing (1811), after the mourning period, he resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 疏陳四川積弊六事，曰：禁科派以安閭閻，除啯匪以防積漸，查卡房以全民命，禁拐騙以警貪頑，嚴攤捐以養廉潔，覈戎政以歸實效。

translations.literal: He memorialized on six longstanding abuses in Sichuan, namely: prohibit irregular levies to secure the people; eliminate gunkou bandits to prevent gradual encroachment; investigate checkpoint stations to protect lives; prohibit kidnapping and fraud to warn the greedy and obstinate; strictly limit surcharges to nurture integrity; and audit military administration to restore real effectiveness.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on six longstanding abuses in Sichuan: ban irregular levies to protect the people; eliminate gunkou bandits before they take root; investigate checkpoint stations to safeguard lives; ban kidnapping and fraud to warn the corrupt; strictly limit surcharges to encourage honest administration; and audit military affairs to restore real effectiveness.

sentences.zh: 又言京師賭風大熾，多屬王公大臣輿夫設局，倚勢骫法，帝命指實，下詔嚴治。

translations.literal: He also stated that gambling in the capital flourished greatly, mostly operated by chair-bearers of princes and great ministers who relied on power to bend the law; the emperor ordered specific identification and issued an edict for stern punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that gambling in the capital had grown rampant, often run by chair-bearers of princes and high ministers who bent the law through their influence; the emperor ordered specific identification and issued an edict for stern punishment.

sentences.zh: 逾日，獲賭案三，大學士、步軍統領祿康輿夫為之魁。

translations.literal: Within a day three gambling cases were uncovered; the chair-bearers of Grand Secretary and Metropolitan Garrison Commander Lukang were the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Within a day three gambling cases were uncovered; the ringleaders proved to be chair-bearers of Grand Secretary and Metropolitan Garrison Commander Lukang.

sentences.zh: 親貴近臣，莫不悚息​​。

translations.literal: Imperial kin and close ministers were all struck with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kin and court favorites were all struck with fear.

sentences.zh: 巡視山東漕務，轉工科給事中、光祿寺少卿，督陝甘學政。

translations.literal: He inspected grain transport affairs in Shandong, was transferred to supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and supervised education in Shaanxi and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected grain transport in Shandong, was transferred to supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and was appointed Commissioner of Education for Shaanxi and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「榆、綏諸州縣倉貯空虛，宜設法籌補，其地資蒙古糧食接濟。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The granaries of Yulin, Suide, and other prefectures and counties are empty and should be replenished by every means; these regions rely on Mongol grain for relief."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The granaries of Yulin, Suide, and other prefectures and counties stand empty and must be replenished; these regions depend on Mongol grain for relief."

sentences.zh: 今腹裡邊外俱荒，當分別安置撫卹。

translations.literal: Now both the interior and the frontier are desolate; they should be separately settled and given relief.
translations.idiomatic: Now both the interior districts and the frontier are devastated; refugees should be settled and relieved according to their circumstances.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「南山善後事宜，宜行堅壁清野之法。

translations.literal: He also stated: "For postwar arrangements in the Southern Mountains, the method of fortified villages and cleared countryside should be applied."
translations.idiomatic: He also stated: "For postwar recovery in the Southern Mountains, the method of fortified villages and cleared countryside should be applied."

sentences.zh: 山內流民雜處，最為奸藪，當嚴行保甲，使姦宄無所匿。

translations.literal: Within the mountains migrant populations are mixed together, forming the greatest nest of villainy; baojia should be strictly enforced so that evildoers have nowhere to hide.
translations.idiomatic: Within the mountains migrant populations are intermingled, forming the greatest nest of villainy; baojia registration should be strictly enforced so evildoers have nowhere to hide.

sentences.zh: 軍中擄脅難民子女，請嚴禁。

translations.literal: Soldiers abduct and coerce refugee women and children; this should be strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers abduct and coerce refugee women and children; this must be strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 南山附近及豫東並經兵燹，宜慎選牧令，以蘇民氣。

translations.literal: The vicinity of the Southern Mountains and eastern Henan have all suffered warfare; magistrates should be carefully selected to revive the people's spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Mountains and eastern Henan have all suffered warfare; magistrates should be carefully chosen to revive the people's morale.

sentences.zh: 川北荒歉，與陝、甘毗連，鹽梟啯匪多出其中，請先事豫防。

translations.literal: Northern Sichuan suffers famine and poor harvests and borders Shaanxi and Gansu; salt smugglers and gunkou bandits mostly emerge from these regions; preventive measures should be taken in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Sichuan suffers famine and borders Shaanxi and Gansu; salt smugglers and gunkou bandits mostly emerge from these regions; preventive measures should be taken in advance.

sentences.zh: 」並下疆吏如所請行。

translations.literal: All were ordered transmitted to frontier officials to implement as requested.
translations.idiomatic: All recommendations were transmitted to provincial officials for implementation.

sentences.zh: 歷鴻臚寺卿、通政司副使、太常寺卿、左副都御史。

translations.literal: He served successively as Director of the Court of Imperial Banquets, Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Director of the Court of Imperial Banquets, Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，命察視近畿水災，督黃村賑務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was ordered to inspect flood disasters in the capital vicinity and supervise relief at Huangcun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing (1819), he was ordered to inspect flood damage near the capital and supervise relief at Huangcun.

sentences.zh: 督福建學政，疏言：「閩中吏治久窳，請不限資格，用廉幹吏補汀、漳、泉三郡望緊要缺，久其任以專責成。

translations.literal: As Fujian Commissioner of Education he memorialized: "Official governance in Fujian has long been corrupt; I request that qualifications not be limited and that honest, capable officials be used to fill key vacancies in the three prefectures of Tingzhou, Zhangzhou, and Quanzhou, with extended terms to fix responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: As Commissioner of Education for Fujian he memorialized: "Official governance in Fujian has long been corrupt; I ask that qualifications be waived and honest, capable men appointed to key posts in Tingzhou, Zhangzhou, and Quanzhou, with extended terms to fix responsibility."

sentences.zh: 漳、泉營伍通盜，請責提鎮立予重典，勿稍袒庇。

translations.literal: Garrisons in Zhangzhou and Quanzhou collude with bandits; I request that regional commanders and brigade generals be held to immediate severe punishment without the slightest shielding.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons in Zhangzhou and Quanzhou collude with bandits; I ask that regional commanders and brigade generals be held to immediate severe punishment without the slightest favoritism.

sentences.zh: 」道光六年，遷倉場侍郎，以病罷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Granary and dismissed on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daoguang (1826), he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Granary and dismissed citing ill health.

sentences.zh: 起補工部侍郎，京察，原品休致。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Works; at the capital evaluation he retired at his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Works; at the capital evaluation he retired at his original rank.

sentences.zh: 卒於家，祀鄉賢祠。

translations.literal: He died at home and was enshrined in the Local Worthies Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home and was enshrined in the hall of local worthies.

sentences.zh: 朱方增，字虹舫，浙江海鹽人。

translations.literal: Zhu Fangzeng, styled Hongfang, was a native of Haiyan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fangzeng, whose style was Hongfang, came from Haiyan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the sixth year of Jiaqing (1801), entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationary scholar, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 典雲南鄉試，遷國子監司業。

translations.literal: He presided over the Yunnan provincial examination and was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief examiner for Yunnan and was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 十八年，教匪之變，方增劾直隸總督溫承惠貽誤地方，黜之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, during the sectarian rebellion, Fangzeng impeached Zhili Governor-General Wen Chenghui for mishandling the region, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Jiaqing (1813), during the White Lotus rebellion, Fangzeng impeached Zhili Governor-General Wen Chenghui for mishandling the province, and Wen was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 應詔陳言，論用人理財，略曰：「近今大臣中，罕有以進賢為務者。

translations.literal: In response to an imperial edict soliciting opinions, he discussed the employment of men and management of finances, stating in summary: "Among great ministers today, few make the advancement of worthy men their task."
translations.idiomatic: In response to an imperial edict soliciting opinions, he discussed appointing officials and managing finances, stating in summary: "Among senior ministers today, few make the advancement of worthy men their chief concern."

sentences.zh: 蓋薦舉之事，易於徇私，黨援交結，不得不防，而大臣亦遂引嫌自避。

translations.literal: For recommendation easily lends itself to favoritism, and factional ties and mutual obligations must be guarded against; thus great ministers also avoid involvement out of scruple.
translations.idiomatic: Recommendation easily lends itself to favoritism, and factional ties must be guarded against; thus senior ministers avoid involvement out of scruple.

sentences.zh: 夫大臣避徇私之名，而忘以人事君之責，所謂因噎廢食，非公忠體國者所宜有也。

translations.literal: For great ministers to avoid the name of favoritism and forget the duty of serving the ruler through men—this is what is called giving up eating for fear of choking; it is not what those who are loyal and public-spirited toward the state should do.
translations.idiomatic: For senior ministers to shun the appearance of favoritism and neglect the duty of serving the ruler through worthy appointments—this is giving up eating for fear of choking; it is not what a loyal servant of the state should do.

sentences.zh: 至於任用之方，則無過於考言詢事。

translations.literal: As for the method of employment, nothing surpasses examining words and inquiring into affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As for the method of appointment, nothing surpasses examining a man's words and testing him on affairs.

sentences.zh: 皇上博訪週諮，徐為印證。

translations.literal: Your Majesty broadly inquires and consults thoroughly, gradually verifying the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty inquires broadly and consults thoroughly, gradually verifying the facts.

sentences.zh: 於召對時，各就所長，諭使面陳，果能洞悉原委，又當試之以事，以觀其能踐與否。

translations.literal: At imperial audiences, each according to his strengths should be instructed to state matters face to face; if he can truly grasp the full circumstances, he should then be tested with affairs to observe whether he can carry them out.
translations.idiomatic: At imperial audiences, each man should be questioned according to his strengths; if he truly grasps the full circumstances, he should then be tested with real duties to see whether he can perform them.

sentences.zh: 如或敷奏並無條理，則其人固不足用，而大臣之識見優絀，心地公私，亦可見矣。

translations.literal: If his presentation lacks all coherence, then the man is certainly unfit for use, and the great minister's discernment, superior or inferior, and whether his heart is public or private, may also be seen.
translations.idiomatic: If a candidate's presentation lacks all coherence, the man is unfit for office, and the recommending minister's judgment and whether his motives are public or private become equally clear.

sentences.zh: 抑臣思臣工居職，苟非闒茸齷齪者流，孰不思自效？

translations.literal: Yet your servant reflects that officials in office, unless they are the incompetent and base sort, who does not wish to serve effectively?
translations.idiomatic: Yet your servant reflects that officials in office, unless they are incompetent and base, who does not wish to serve effectively?

sentences.zh: 況蒙皇上訓飭至再至三，而猶故習相仍，驟難振拔者，良有數端：條例過繁，文案蒨屑，雖有強敏之吏，而精神疲於具文，其實關於政治民生，轉致不能詳覈。

translations.literal: Moreover, though admonished by Your Majesty again and again, old habits continue and sudden reform is difficult—there are truly several reasons: regulations are excessively numerous and documents trivially minute; even capable officials find their energy exhausted by paperwork, and matters that truly concern governance and the people's livelihood consequently cannot be thoroughly examined.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though admonished by Your Majesty again and again, old habits persist and sudden reform is difficult—for several reasons: regulations are excessively numerous and paperwork trivially minute; even capable officials find their energy exhausted by documents, and matters that truly concern governance and the people's livelihood cannot be thoroughly examined.

sentences.zh: 一也。

translations.literal: This is the first.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first.

sentences.zh: 差務絡繹，公私賠累，身家之卹不遑，民物之懷漸恝。

translations.literal: Dispatch duties come in endless succession, with public and private losses; there is no leisure to care for one's household, and concern for the people's welfare gradually grows indifferent.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch duties come in endless succession, draining public and private resources; officials have no leisure to care for their households, and concern for the people's welfare gradually fades.

sentences.zh: 二也。

translations.literal: This is the second.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second.

sentences.zh: 訐告之風，至今益甚。

translations.literal: The fashion of accusation grows worse to this day.
translations.idiomatic: The culture of malicious accusation grows worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 嘗有以田土、鬥毆細故而叩閽京控者，有司畏其挾制，不得不姑息委蛇。

translations.literal: There have been cases where trifling disputes over fields or brawls were brought to the capital for appeal; local officials fear being coerced and cannot but temporize and yield.
translations.idiomatic: Men have appealed to the capital over trifling land disputes or brawls; local officials fear being coerced and cannot but temporize.

sentences.zh: 雖有急公自好者，其尋常蒨屑之事，豈皆一一可達聖聰？

translations.literal: Even those who are public-spirited and self-respecting—can every trivial matter reach the sacred ear?
translations.idiomatic: Even public-spirited officials cannot bring every trivial matter before the throne.

sentences.zh: 甚至匿名揭帖，無主名之可指。

translations.literal: Some even post anonymous placards with no name that can be identified.
translations.idiomatic: Some even post anonymous placards with no name to identify.

sentences.zh: 蠹吏猾胥，奸民惡僕，求謀不遂，懲治過嚴，皆可造作飛語，訐及陰私。

translations.literal: Corrupt officials, cunning runners, wicked commoners, and vicious servants whose schemes fail or who are punished too severely can all fabricate slander and accuse private matters.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt officials, cunning runners, wicked commoners, and vicious servants whose schemes fail or who are punished too harshly can all fabricate slander touching private matters.

sentences.zh: 足使任事之心，不寒而栗，委曲隱忍。

translations.literal: This is enough to make the heart of one who takes on affairs shiver without cold and submit in compromise and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: This is enough to make officials who take on real duties shiver with dread and submit in compromise.

sentences.zh: 姦宄橫行，大都由此。

translations.literal: The rampant spread of villainy is mostly due to this.
translations.idiomatic: The rampant spread of villainy stems largely from this.

sentences.zh: 三也。

translations.literal: This is the third.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third.

sentences.zh: 今皇上欲整飭因循積習，臣愚以為必先除此三者之弊，庶廓然無所疑畏，而得專精實政矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty wishes to rectify longstanding habits of routine indulgence; your servant humbly considers that these three abuses must first be removed, so that all may be clear without doubt or fear, and real administration may be pursued with full concentration.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty wishes to rectify longstanding habits of routine indulgence; your servant humbly holds that these three abuses must be removed first, so that officials may act without fear and devote themselves fully to real administration.

sentences.zh: 經國之方，理財尤要。

translations.literal: In governing the state, financial management is especially important.
translations.idiomatic: In governing the state, financial management is especially important.

sentences.zh: 古者以三十年之通制國用，斟酌盈虛，量入為出，用能經常不匱。

translations.literal: In antiquity a thirty-year comprehensive plan governed state expenditure, balancing surplus and deficit and measuring outgo by income, thereby maintaining regular sufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity a thirty-year comprehensive budget governed state expenditure, balancing surplus and deficit and measuring outgo by income, thereby maintaining regular sufficiency.

sentences.zh: 今戶部歲入歲出，年一匯奏。

translations.literal: Today the Ministry of Revenue's annual income and expenditure are reported once a year in summary.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Ministry of Revenue reports annual income and expenditure once a year in summary.

sentences.zh: 惟中外未合為一，條緒繁賾，極難釐剔。

translations.literal: Yet capital and provinces are not combined into one account; the threads are numerous and tangled, making thorough sorting extremely difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Yet capital and provincial accounts are not combined; the records are numerous and tangled, making thorough auditing extremely difficult.

sentences.zh: 且凡撥解即謂之出，並未實計所用。

translations.literal: Moreover, whatever is allocated and forwarded is counted as expenditure without actually calculating what was used.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, whatever is allocated is counted as expenditure without calculating what was actually spent.

sentences.zh: 新舊牽溷，凌雜益甚，而出納諸款，又因有無定之款，盈朒參差。

translations.literal: Old and new accounts are entangled and confusion grows worse; receipts and disbursements further vary because of uncertain items, with surpluses and deficits uneven.
translations.idiomatic: Old and new accounts are entangled and confusion grows worse; receipts and disbursements further vary because of uncertain items, with surpluses and deficits unevenly reported.

sentences.zh: 以故一歲之中，所出幾何，覈之所入，贏餘若干，不能得其實數。

translations.literal: Thus within a single year how much was spent, how much received when verified, and how much surplus remained cannot be known in real figures.
translations.idiomatic: Thus within a single year how much was spent, how much received, and how much surplus remained cannot be known in real figures.

sentences.zh: 請旨敕下戶部，歲入歲出，宜合中外為一。

translations.literal: I request an imperial order to the Ministry of Revenue that annual income and expenditure should combine capital and provinces into one account.
translations.idiomatic: I request an imperial order to the Ministry of Revenue to combine capital and provincial income and expenditure into a single account.

sentences.zh: 核計贏餘總數，仍取前一二歲所贏餘，確實比較，然後審其輕重緩急，舉一切例內例外諸用款，有可裁省停緩者，酌加撙節。

translations.literal: Calculate the total surplus, still taking the surpluses of the previous one or two years for reliable comparison, then weigh what is light or heavy, urgent or deferred, and for all expenditures within and outside precedent, where reduction or deferral is possible, add appropriate economy.
translations.idiomatic: Calculate the total surplus, compare it reliably with surpluses from the previous one or two years, then weigh priorities and, for all routine and exceptional expenditures, reduce or defer what can be cut.

sentences.zh: 庶合於古人通年制用之法，而度支充裕矣。

translations.literal: Thus it may accord with the ancient method of comprehensive annual budgeting, and state expenditure will be ample.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the state may follow the ancient method of comprehensive annual budgeting, and the treasury will be ample.

sentences.zh: 二十年，入直懋勤殿，編纂石渠寶笈、秘殿珠林。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he entered duty in the Hall of Exertion in Diligence and compiled the Stone Canal Precious Collection and the Secret Hall Pearl Forest.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Jiaqing (1815), he took up duty in the Hall of Exertion in Diligence and compiled the Stone Canal Precious Collection and the Secret Hall Pearl Forest.

sentences.zh: 尋督廣西學政，累遷翰林院侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Soon after he supervised education in Guangxi and was promoted in succession to Hanlin reader in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Commissioner of Education for Guangxi and rose to Reader in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，大考第一，擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang, at the triennial evaluation he ranked first and was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daoguang (1824), at the triennial palace examination evaluation he ranked first and was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 典山東鄉試。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shandong provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief examiner for Shandong's provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 七年，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he supervised education in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daoguang (1827), he was appointed Commissioner of Education for Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Daoguang (1830).

sentences.zh: 方增熟諳朝章典故，輯國史名臣事蹟，為從政觀法錄，行於世。

translations.literal: Fangzeng was thoroughly versed in court regulations and historical precedents; he compiled the deeds of eminent ministers in the national histories into Records for Observing Models in Governance, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Fangzeng was thoroughly versed in court regulations and historical precedent; he compiled the deeds of eminent ministers from the dynastic histories into Records for Observing Models in Governance, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 論曰：萬承風、周系英、錢樾以侍從之臣，軺車所至，建白卓然。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Wan Chengfeng, Zhou Xiying, and Qian Yue, as attendant ministers, wherever their inspection carriages went, offered outstanding proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal states: As palace attendants, Wan Chengfeng, Zhou Xiying, and Qian Yue offered outstanding proposals wherever their inspection tours took them.

sentences.zh: 秦瀛之治績，李宗瀚之孝行，非僅以文藻稱。

translations.literal: Qin Ying's administrative achievements and Li Zonghan's filial conduct were not praised merely for literary ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Ying's administrative achievements and Li Zonghan's filial devotion were acclaimed for more than literary talent alone.

sentences.zh: 韓鼎晉、朱方增侃侃獻納，言有體要，皆風采著於朝列矣。

translations.literal: Han Dingjin and Zhu Fangzeng presented their views frankly and earnestly, their words having substance and point; all displayed distinguished bearing in the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Han Dingjin and Zhu Fangzeng offered their views frankly and earnestly, with words of substance and point; all displayed distinguished bearing among their colleagues at court.
